boundaries: One local macOS host; four exact client binaries and the identified uncommitted Locust artifacts. No packaged installation or cross-machine qualification.

Normal launch/resume uses deliberately permissive authored client settings. Default-policy blocking and intentional crash recovery are separate scenarios; final campaign uses candidate 5, with candidate 3 retained as historical evidence.
Ordinary scoped tools and explicit local resume are covered; active hooks, automatic wake, confinement and unattended activation are not qualified.

Notification and process exit do not acknowledge cancellation. Normal runs explicitly acknowledged an uncertain executor outcome through the authenticated API; result acceptance and integration were outside these runs.
Normal cleanup covers the owned managed process/session and bridges identified by protected receipts. Fully detached descendants lacking matching receipts are outside that evidence.
Fault recovery intentionally SIGKILLs the retained managed parent and later forces owned fault cleanup. This is not natural fault-cleanup evidence.

Private runtime paths, prompts, environment values, configuration contents, credential/session-secret bytes and native transcripts are omitted. Opaque transcript and report digests remain for correlation.

A later retained-output-pipe fix is also outside these artifacts: final source observes direct-child exit independently of descendant-held pipe EOF. These runs qualify the measured ordinary cleanup scenarios, not that new regression fix.

Candidate 4 corrected the candidate 3 Codex snapshot race. Historical candidate 3 recovery and candidate 4 normal runs precede repeated-signal and retained-pipe fixes; final candidate 5 campaigns include both fixes. Scripted client campaigns do not independently exercise every component regression.
capability_encoding: Enabled capability names list exactly the true values from tools, active_delivery, idle_wake, manual_resume, recovery, confinement; omitted names are false.
